title: About and support

fields.heading: About LabRats
fields.lead: Who we are, how we teach, and the help available so every family can afford real science.
fields.description: About San Diego LabRats, a 501(c)(3) nonprofit in Carlsbad - our mission, impact, team, teaching philosophy, scholarships, charter school funding, press, and flyers.

body:
Who we are

To make advanced STEM learning accessible, engaging, and exciting for all kids, no matter their zip code.

San Diego LabRats is a where working scientists teach hands-on science to kids in grades K-8. Our teachers love their fields and love teaching the next generation; we use hands-on lab curriculum and current techniques, and we bring the fun back to learning science.

Our goal is to offer the program to underserved kids throughout San Diego County, which is only possible with our community's support.

Our home is the STEM Discovery Center at , , , and our Mobile STEAM Lab visits schools and events across the county. Get directions

2023-24 in numbers

From our annual impact report, across our three programs: the STEM Discovery Center, the Mobile Lab, and STEM at Home online lessons.

3,000+Children and families served
$450,000Subsidized across all classes
1,350Students in afterschool programs
900Students in camps
2,250Students served by the Mobile Lab
1 to 5Days a week the Discovery Center is open

We also added 9 charter school partners and 2 San Diego school district partners, mentored 8 high school interns, and were finalists for two community awards: Social Impact Nonprofit Charity of the Year and Nonprofit Social Impact Changemakers of the Year. Read the full report (PDF)

The staff is very attuned to the children's interests. They treat them like young scientists, they're very respectful, and the environment is set up so that children are naturally drawn to wanting to tinker, ask questions, and explore.

Pilar Bewley, retired teacher and homeschool parent

Working with LabRats has doubled in developing my skills as a person and scientist. I've been able to learn how to teach and contribute in a professional environment (and learn how to do my taxes). Between revisiting labs from my childhood, making an impact in every student I meet, and connecting with fellow teachers, I've been able to pass down a love for STEM in ways I never thought possible.

Adora, high school intern

Quotes from the 2023-24 impact report, with spelling and punctuation corrected.

Team: scientists teaching science

  • Jason Merrill

    Executive Director

  • Dr. Shawn Carlson

    Chief Science Officer

    "Dr. Shawn" earned bachelor's degrees in physics and applied mathematics at UC Berkeley (1981), then a master's in physics (1983) and a Ph.D. in nuclear physics (1989) at UCLA. He left academic research in 1993 to find new ways to inspire young people to love STEM, work that earned him a MacArthur Fellowship in 1999. He is a nationally known science writer and the creative mind behind LabRats.

    In 2008 he codified his approach as Engagement Education, which works in three spheres: students commit to their own education, learning communities form where students support each other, and students and teachers build strong bonds through character as well as academics. LabRats teaches STEM this way.

  • J. Ryan Merrill

    Vice President and Director of Education

    Ryan earned a master's in chemistry at the University of Colorado Boulder (2015), researching organic polymers under Professor Christopher Bowman, and a bachelor's in chemistry at UC Santa Barbara (2013), with more than three years of research on mass spectrometry and the proteins involved in type 2 diabetes under Professor Michael Bowers.

    He taught general chemistry classes and labs at the University of Colorado for two years and has tutored STEM classes for more than six years. He grew up in Encinitas, attended LCCHS, and gives back to the community he loves by developing curriculum, teaching labs, and running demonstrations for local kids.

How we teach

Kids learn best by doing, especially when they chase their own ideas with someone more knowledgeable nearby. Project-based learning builds critical thinking, problem solving, teamwork, and self-management.

Our teachers are scientists who have done their own research. They turn textbook ideas into hands-on labs tied to the real world, showing students that science built the modern marvels around them. Everything we do builds a growth mindset: labs push kids to think problems through rather than follow directions, and when a student asks "what if," we say "let's try it." Kids learn that not understanding something at first doesn't mean they never will, and they gain the confidence to keep going instead of shutting down. Like sports teams and scouting, classes build community through teamwork and friendly competition: dynamic and fun, not "sit and listen."

An education in science and technology is nothing less than the power to transform the world with a single idea. The modern world was built by hundreds of thousands of people who understood how nature works and solved practical problems; a few made incredible contributions, most made modest ones, and every one of them knew they had made a difference.

Read more: Why learn science? and Our teaching methods

The LabRats Code of Honor

  1. Be fair, kind, and generous to all
  2. Respect yourself and all others
  3. Never cheat or accept the cheating of others
  4. Think like a scientist
  5. Always do the smart thing
  6. Always follow through
  7. Work for a higher purpose

The LabRats motto

Investigate. Do the experiment!

Students don't have to rely on what someone else tells them is true. They have the power to discover the truth for themselves, and we encourage them to use it every day.

Built for homeschool and independent study

We build our curriculum and services around what homeschool and independent-study students need. Real scientists teach, students are encouraged to ask questions, and hands-on experiments show scientific principles in action instead of only on the page. In our collaborative labs, your child will:

  • Explore science tools, games, and puzzles
  • Meet other young scientists at the Discovery Center

body:
Engagement Education

Our approach is called Engagement Education: scientists teaching science in ways that are fun and engaging. It helps students build character, self-confidence, and a real passion for what they learn. The goal is an encouraging STEAM education that helps every kid find their passion and do their best.

Enrichment courses

Multi-week courses for three age bands: K-2, 3-5, and 6-8. We fit the curriculum to each school, with hands-on labs of an hour or more to suit your students' schedule.

Topics range from NGSS physical and life science, like electricity, magnetism, DNA, and digestion, to subjects kids will need for the future: coding, robotics, and forensics.

Workshops

One-time sessions using our Mobile Lab, which can deliver any of our 100+ hands-on lessons to your classroom or event. We can also help scout troops earn the STEM merit badge.

Every lab gets students running experiments with their own hands, with simple demonstrations of advanced ideas.

Who teaches

Courses are taught by working scientists, including Dr. Shawn Carlson, a nuclear physicist and nationally known science writer, and J. Ryan Merrill, a chemist who taught chemistry classes and labs at the University of Colorado Boulder.

Meet the team

body:
Ever wondered what happens when real science meets hands-on tinkering? Bring your family to see the STEM Discovery Center. Whether your child is an aspiring engineer, a budding biologist, or just loves to build and test things, the center is built to spark imagination and critical thinking.

During your one-hour tour

  • Demos of the makerspace tools, build stations, and creative projects
  • Mini experiments, engineering challenges, and hands-on science stations for kids
  • Early access to upcoming class schedules, special event discounts, and Q&A with our leadership team

Why timed entry?

Tours run in one-hour blocks so every family gets real time at the workbenches without crowding. Space in each block is limited. Choose your day and time in the registration form.

body:
Real scientists teaching science.

Hands-on labs for kids in grades K-8 at our STEM Discovery Center in Carlsbad. Every class is taught by a working scientist, and every kid gets to be a kid.

See the schedule and register Browse programs

, · ·

Two hours, two halves

Afterschool sessions at the STEM Discovery Center run in two parts. First a scientist leads a one-hour lab. Then kids get an hour of open maker space to build, test, and dig into whatever caught their interest.

Classes meet Tuesday through Saturday in two groups: grades K-3 and grades 4-8. New lessons every week.

How afterschool works

Hour 1
Teacher-led lab. A scientist walks the group through a hands-on experiment.
Hour 2
Open maker space. Kids choose what to build, test, or explore with our supplies.

Sign up

Ways to enroll

Holiday break campsThanksgiving and winter break, half daysCamp dates

Our philosophy

Investigate. Do the experiment!

Kids need a place where they can explore, ask questions, and get their hands dirty, with a mentor who knows the material. Our teachers are scientists who love their field and love teaching it. Every lab ties an idea from the textbook to something real.

title: Our teaching methods

fields.lead: We aim to inspire kids to love learning science, and to motivate them to do the work it takes to become truly competent in STEM.
fields.description: How San Diego LabRats teaches - self, social, and custodial engagement, learner-centered courses, and scientists as role models.

body:
Three kinds of engagement

Our teaching develops self, social, and custodial engagement. It helps kids discover their passions, build strong friendships and sportsmanship, and meet role models from the scientific community.

Our learner-centered courses and camps deepen each student's interest in science and technology, with a curriculum as flexible and varied as our students' interests and talents.

Self engagement

Education research suggests the most effective way to improve academic performance is to meet the intellectual and emotional needs of students as individuals, rather than chase higher average test scores across large groups.

Overcoming life's obstacles takes grit. We work to build in each student a lasting commitment to becoming literate in STEM, using proven practices from cognitive psychology to help kids truly master STEM content and develop scientific habits of mind.

Social engagement

People tend to succeed when family and close friends support them. So we build friendship and sportsmanship into the program, and students support each other while working toward a shared goal.

Custodial engagement

We give students the best role models the scientific community has: scientists teaching science from the ground up, not starting in college. Our mentors know from experience what it takes to earn a science degree and what it means to be a scientist. They teach the commitment it takes to succeed in science, and the ethical standards the scientific community depends on.

body:
What happens in a session

The STEM Discovery Center is a place to discover, create, build, and dive into science, with the freedom to follow your own curiosity.

Each two-hour session starts with a one-hour course led by a real scientist. Then comes an hour of open maker space, set up by our staff, where kids build, test, and explore the topics that interest them most. There's a new lesson every week.

The program uses Engagement Education: kids commit to their own learning, support each other as a group, and learn from scientists who care about character as much as content. How we teach

Hour 1
Teacher-led lab with a working scientist
Hour 2
Open maker space to build, create, and explore

Inside the Discovery Center

Each lab starts with a short classroom lecture by one of our scientists on a specific topic, followed by a hands-on experiment. We rotate labs regularly from our library of curriculum.

In open maker space, kids explore whatever they're curious about: games, experiments, and engineering challenges, using everything in the center.

What's in the center

  • Compound and stereo microscopes
  • A slime station for building any kind of slime
  • Lego robots to build and code
  • A magnetic marble run to build your own track
  • Messy labs: two creative labs, rotated regularly
  • A maker space tower with materials for engineering projects, like a balloon-powered car

In the lab

body:
You don't need a million-dollar lab

Science is the process we use to study the world around us and make sure we aren't fooling ourselves. It happens everywhere, and you can do it with simple, cheap materials. These labs are designed for friends and families to do together at home.

Safety first: some labs are dangerous and need a parent to supervise or take part.

Video labs

  • Science of flight: Bernoulli's principle

  • Science of light: build your own spectroscope

  • Light and the electromagnetic spectrum

  • How plants cover the Earth: seed dispersal

  • 5 science experiments for grades K-3

  • Spooky Halloween science

  • 6 at-home experiments for grades 4-8

Thanks to Brainstem Creative for helping us produce these videos.

More free labs on BrainSTEMtv

BrainSTEMtv offers free at-home lessons whenever your schedule allows, from SDLabRats, the San Diego Botanic Garden, Studio Ace Art, and more.

title: Sensational Science Camp

fields.heading: Sensational Science Camp: explore the world through your senses
fields.description: LabRats Sensational Science summer camp in Carlsbad. Kids explore how their senses detect the world, and the science of balance.

body:
A summer camp about the science of the human senses. Your senses are like built-in scientific instruments, and campers explore how their bodies detect and interpret the world around them.

Kids also dig into the science of balance: not just how we stay upright, but how balance matters in engineering everything from medicine coolers to chemical processes.

See other summer STEM camps.

title: Forensic Science Camp

fields.heading: Forensic Science Camp: the science behind solving crimes
fields.description: LabRats Forensic Science summer camp in Carlsbad. Kids collect fingerprints, test mystery substances, and crack cases with real forensic techniques.

body:
It's like a crime show, but without the crime. At Forensic Science Camp, kids become scientific sleuths and learn how real forensic scientists use evidence to solve mysteries. Your child will:

  • Collect and analyze fingerprints using professional techniques
  • Examine mysterious substances with chemical analysis
  • Decipher secret messages with forensic tools
  • Work with teammates to solve mysteries

The curriculum is written by real scientists who know how to make forensic concepts engaging and age-appropriate. Along the way, kids build critical thinking, scientific reasoning, and attention to detail that help them in school and beyond.

See other summer STEM camps.

title: Why learn science?

fields.lead: The power of science comes from understanding both the facts and the process people use to discover them.
fields.description: Why San Diego LabRats teaches science - what science is, what doing science is about, and what makes a scientist a scientist.

body:
What is science?

Science is everything we know about the physical universe, and how we know it.

That restates the "systemized body of knowledge" definition usually taught in school, and it makes clear that science is both the facts and the process used to discover them.

What is doing science about?

Making sure you're not fooling yourself.

That is the heart of the scientific enterprise: each scientist working painstakingly to avoid fooling themselves. If you don't know how to check whether you're fooling yourself, you're more likely to be fooled. We teach students that reasoned self-skepticism gives them a big advantage in every part of life.

Science isn't just one way to understand nature. It's the best approach we have to understanding the physical universe.

What makes a scientist a scientist?

Always fit theories to facts, never facts to theories.

We all have beliefs. Many people, faced with facts that contradict a belief, bend their reading of the facts to fit what they want to believe. A scientist makes a personal commitment to a worldview where the truth matters more than any belief they hold right now.

A scientist stays skeptical of their own ideas and is willing to change them when credible evidence shows they're wrong.

title: Winter STEAM Discovery Camp 2021

fields.heading: TING presents: Winter STEAM Discovery Camp
fields.lead: An in-person winter break camp at the San Diego Botanic Garden in Encinitas, with two sessions over the 2021 holidays.
fields.description: The 2021 TING Winter STEAM Discovery Camp at the San Diego Botanic Garden - Life of Plants, Creative Chemistry, Forensic Science, and Secret Agent Science.
fields.archive_note: This camp ran from December 27, 2021 to January 7, 2022.

body:
Session 1
December 27–31, 2021
Session 2
January 3–7, 2022
Hours
9:00 am–12:00 pm (drop-off 8:30–9:00, pick-up 12:00–12:30)
Where
San Diego Botanic Garden, Junior Quail Trail, 300 Quail Gardens Dr., Encinitas, CA 92024
Registration donation
$275

Both weeks offered the same camp. Camp was held outdoors under tents; campers wore closed-toe shoes and jackets and brought their own snacks and water. Thanks to TING, extra scholarships were available for the rest of 2021.

Grades K-3

Life of Plants

Young horticulturalists looked at the world from a plant's point of view. By observing the plants and pollinators around them, students got an introduction to the scientific method and learned where plants came from and how they live with their environment. No green thumb required.

Creative Chemistry

From instant chemical reactions to DIY slime, a creative introduction to chemistry, the study of matter. Using safe compounds from around the house and kitchen, students explored chemical reactions and the properties used to describe matter.

Grades 4-8

Secret Agent Science

Every spy needs a gadget person. Students learned techniques from chemistry to computer science: sending secret messages with chemistry, coding messages only they could read, and using those skills to solve a treasure hunt.

Forensic Science

It's like a crime show, but without the crime. Students learned how scientists examine a "crime" scene and find useful evidence with fingerprinting and chemical analysis.
